Definition: , including the irregular feminine μηδεμία, and the neuter μηδέν from G3361 and G1520; not even one (man, woman, thing):--any (man, thing), no (man), none, not (at all, any man, a whit), nothing, + without delay.
BiblicalUsage: The word means no one, nothing, and it is the absolute negative of the New Testament: Jesus tells the healed leper to tell no man, and the demon is commanded to hold its peace and come out of the man. Paul says recompense to no man evil for evil.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word draws a line with no exceptions: tell no man, and pay back no man evil for evil — because the God who commands it is the one who provides for it.
